_meta.note: T-13 (eval-committee-deterministic-validators plan, Phase 4): a NATIVE, deliberately lightweight regex-based security anti-pattern check for aios-eval's C-W1 'Security Vulnerabilities' criterion (Sarah Winters, Security & Trust domain). This is NOT a port of ai-os-jc-toast's bandit_security.py/semgrep_security.py - confirmed by a repo-wide grep for 'bandit', 'semgrep', and 'SEC-' before writing this file that aios-eval has zero existing SAST infrastructure (no baseline-findings.json, no bandit/semgrep dependency, no prior SEC-* check anywhere). Building a full bandit/semgrep-equivalent SAST tool from scratch for one criterion in one cron cycle would be disproportionate scope, so this is a scoped-down regex sweep over 2 anti-pattern families instead: hardcoded secrets/credentials (SEC-001) and dangerous dynamic execution/shell injection (SEC-003).
_meta.naming_rationale: check_id numbers SEC-001 and SEC-003 are deliberately chosen to align with ai-os-jc-toast's own bandit_security.py catalogue naming for the SAME anti-pattern families (that module's own mapping table: B105/106/107 hardcoded-password variants -> SEC-001; B602/604/605/606/607/307 shell-injection & eval variants -> SEC-003) - for cross-repo readability only. The detection MECHANISM here is independent (plain regex over artifact text, no AST/taint-flow analysis) and has a different, generally noisier false-positive/false-negative profile than a real SAST tool.
_meta.known_gaps: No coverage for SQL injection (SEC-002), weak/broken crypto (SEC-005), path traversal (SEC-006), insecure deserialization (SEC-007), SSRF (SEC-008), or XSS (SEC-004) - those categories need AST/taint-flow analysis to check with any precision; a bare regex sweep over prose/code text would be close to pure noise for them. Scoped to the 2 families a text pattern can catch with reasonable (not perfect) precision. Also: this scan cannot distinguish real dangerous code from prose that merely DISCUSSES these patterns (e.g. a security-education SKILL.md saying 'avoid using eval()' would false-positive on SEC-003) - a known limitation inherent to text-pattern matching without context/AST awareness, disclosed here rather than silently tolerated.
